He was selected as the 34th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] after playing three seasons of college basketball for the [[University of Kansas]]. Chalmers was named the 2006–07 Co-Defensive Player of the Year and the [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]] of the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]{{cite news|title=Chalmers signs deal with Heat|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2008/jul/10/chalmers_signs_deal_heat/|work=KUSports.com|date=July 10, 2008|access-date=July 16, 2009}} after winning the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2008 NCAA championship]].{{cite news|title=After 20-year drought, Kansas rallies to beat Memphis for NCAA title|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000063|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170224003150/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=284000063|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 24, 2017|publisher=ESPN|date=April 8, 2008|access-date=April 8, 2009}} In the NBA, he was the starting point guard for two championship-winning teams with the [[Miami Heat]] in [[2012 NBA Finals|2012]] and [[2013 NBA Finals|2013]]. Chalmers is the only Alaskan to win a championship in the high school, college, and pro levels. After seven seasons with the Heat he was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in November 2015 and waived in March 2016 due to injury. After missing a season due to injury he returned with the team in the 2017 offseason before going overseas and G-League in 2018. ==Family life== Mario is the son of Ronnie and Almarie Chalmers, parents who have each played active roles in developing basketball players. Ronnie Chalmers is a former head basketball coach at [[Bartlett High School (Alaska)|Bartlett High School]] and assistant coach at the University of Kansas.{{Cite web|last=Peters|first=Jeremy|date=2011-08-11|title=Miami Heat player brings b-ball camp to Alaska|url=https://www.deseret.com/2011/8/11/20209062/miami-heat-player-brings-b-ball-camp-to-alaska|access-date=2021-04-08|website=Deseret News|language=en}} Almarie Mosley Chalmers has coached many basketball camps and has written a book about raising a basketball family titled ''The Ball is in Your Court: Embracing Your Child's Dreams.'' Chalmers has an older sister named Roneka, who lives in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]], where the Chalmers family lived for some time. Chalmers is the father of four kids. He has three sons named Zachiah A'mario Chalmers, Prynce Almario Chalmers, and one that has an unknown public name. In addition, Chalmers has a daughter named Queen Elizabeth Chalmers.{{cite web|date=January 19, 2012|title=MARIO CHALMERS HAS A DAUGHTER NAMED "QUEEN ELIZABETH"|url=http://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/mario-chalmers-has-a-daughter-named-queen-elizabeth-6556862|access-date=January 19, 2012|work=MiamiNewTimes.com}} He is the cousin of former [[Los Angeles Clippers]] guard [[Lionel Chalmers]], and former Minnesota Timberwolves guard [[Chris Smith (basketball, born 1970)|Chris Smith]]. Chalmers attended [[Bartlett High School (Anchorage, Alaska)|Bartlett High School]] in [[Anchorage, Alaska]], where he was named the 4A State Player of the Year three times in a row, joining [[Trajan Langdon]] as the only other player to receive such acclaim. Chalmers led his high school team to two state championships in 2002 and 2003, and a runner-up finish in 2004. As a senior in 2004–05, he was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] as well as a third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Chalmers was listed as the No. 2 point guard and the No. 12 player in the nation in 2005.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/tamu/basketball/recruiting/player-Mario-Chalmers-20034|title=Mario Chalmers – Yahoo! Sports|work=Yahoo.com|access-date=April 24, 2008}} ==College career== [[File:Mario-Chalmers-KU-vs-UT-Feb-11-08.jpg|thumb|upright|Chalmers playing for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]] in February 2008.]] Chalmers considered [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] and [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] before finally committing to the [[University of Kansas]] on May 21, 2004. Chalmers began his college career on the bench behind guard Jeff Hawkins, but worked his way into the starting rotation in January 2006. He finished the season starting 21 of the final 22 games (missing only senior night). He finished his freshman year averaging 11.5 points per game, which was second highest on the team. He became the second freshman in Big 12 history to win Conference Player of the Week honors and was named National Freshman of the Week twice. He also set the KU and [[Big 12 Conference]] record for most steals in a season by a freshman with 89. Chalmers was named to the Big 12 All-Rookie Team, Big 12 All-Defensive Team, All-Big 12 Honorable Mention (Coaches), Third-Team All-Big-12 ([[Associated Press|AP]]), Big 12 All-Tournament Team and the Big 12 Tournament MVP after helping Kansas win the [[2006 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]]. In 33 games, he also averaged 2.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 2.7 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/mario-chalmers-1.html|title=Mario Chalmers Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=April 24, 2008}} Chalmers was second on the team in scoring with 12.3 points per game as a sophomore, recording four 20-point games during the 2006–07 season. In the Big 12 Coaches Awards, Chalmers was named Co-Defensive Player of the Year with Marcus Dove of [[Oklahoma State Cowboys men's basketball|Oklahoma State]]. He also earned third-team All-Big 12 and All-Big 12 Defensive Team honors. His season total of 97 steals put him in first place in Kansas basketball history for steals in a single season. Chalmers averaged 12.8 points per game during his junior year. He also led the team with 4.3 assists per game, 46.8% three-point shooting accuracy, and 97 steals. His 97 steals tied the school's single season record, a record that he set as a sophomore. He scored 30 points in Kansas' win in the Big 12 Conference tournament title game against [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]]. Chalmers was again named to the Big 12 All-Defensive Team, and earned second-team All-Big 12 honors.{{cite web|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=147|title=Mario Chalmers – 2005–06 Men's Basketball|work=KUAthletics.com|access-date=April 24, 2008}} Chalmers helped his team win the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#National Championship Game|2008 NCAA Championship]] with a three-point shot with 2.1 seconds left in the final game. His three just before the end of regulation brought the game into overtime, where Kansas took over and defeated the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]], led by phenom freshman [[Derrick Rose]]. Chalmers was named [[NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]] of the tournament. It was the Jayhawks' fifth national title (including two pre-tournament titles in 1922 and 1923). In April 2008, Chalmers declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final year of college eligibility.{{cite web|url=http://www2.ljworld.com/photos/galleries/2008/apr/24/mario_chalmers_press_conference/|title=Mario Chalmers' Press Conference|work=LJWorld.com|date=April 24, 2008|access-date=April 24, 2008|archive-date=October 10, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081010210224/http://www2.ljworld.com/photos/galleries/2008/apr/24/mario_chalmers_press_conference/|url-status=dead}} On February 16, 2013, the University of Kansas basketball program retired his jersey, #15.{{cite web|first=Christian|last=Corona|url=http://collegesportsblog.dallasnews.com/2013/02/former-kansas-star-mario-chalmers-has-his-jersey-retired-at-halftime-of-texas-game.html/|title=Former Kansas star Mario Chalmers has his jersey retired at halftime of Texas game|work=DallasNews.com|date=February 16, 2013|access-date=February 16, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130219004736/http://collegesportsblog.dallasnews.com/2013/02/former-kansas-star-mario-chalmers-has-his-jersey-retired-at-halftime-of-texas-game.html/|archive-date=February 19, 2013}} {|class="wikitable" !Year !Games Played !Minutes/Game !Points/Game !Rebounds/Game !Assists/Game !Turnovers/Game !Assist/Turnover !Steals/Game !Steals/Season |- |[[2005–06 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2005–06]] |33 |26.0 |11.5 |2.2 |3.8 |2.8 |1.37 |2.7 |89 |- |[[2006–07 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2006–07]] |38 |29.2 |12.2 |3.0 |3.3 |2.4 |1.36 |2.6 |97 |- |[[2007–08 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|2007–08]] |39 |30.0 |12.8 |3.1 |4.3 |1.9 |2.25 |2.5 |97 |} ==Professional career== ===Miami Heat (2008–2015)=== After working out for 13 teams, Chalmers was drafted with the 34th overall pick in the second round of the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. When asked immediately after being drafted how many times he had watched his overtime-forcing three-pointer against [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] in the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA championship]], Chalmers responded, "a million times." The rights to Chalmers were later included in a trade with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_acquire_chalmers080626.html|title=HEAT Acquire Draft Rights To Mario Chalmers|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2008|access-date=June 26, 2008}} The Heat signed him on July 8. On September 3, 2008, Chalmers and fellow former Kansas Jayhawks teammate [[Darrell Arthur]] were excused from the NBA's rookie transition program. Fellow NBA rookie [[Michael Beasley]] was not asked to leave the camp, but was later fined $50,000 for his involvement in the incident.{{cite web|title=Beasley fined $50,000 for involvement in Rookie Transition Program incident|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3596442|publisher=ESPN|date=September 18, 2008|access-date=June 29, 2014}} ====2008–09 season==== Chalmers started all 82 regular season games his rookie year{{cite web|first=Ira |last=Winderman |url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/basketball/heat/sfl-flspheatnote26sbmar26,0,3698061.story |title=Chalmers 'earned' shot at 82 starts |access-date=March 26, 2009 |date=March 26, 2009 |work=Sun-Sentinel.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090329084031/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/basketball/heat/sfl-flspheatnote26sbmar26%2C0%2C3698061.story |archive-date=March 29, 2009 }} and finished the season averaging 10 points, 4.9 assists, 2.8 rebounds, 2 steals, and 32 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/chalmma01.html|title=Mario Chalmers NBA Stats|access-date=November 5, 2008|work=Basketball-Reference.com}} His two steals per game ranked number one among all rookies and the fourth highest among all players. On November 5, 2008, in just his fourth NBA game, Chalmers set a franchise record for steals in a game with nine.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=281105014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161006151102/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=281105014|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 6, 2016|title=Chalmers gets team-record nine steals in win over Sixers|access-date=November 5, 2008|date=November 5, 2008|publisher=ESPN}} ====2009–10 season==== After having not missed a game up until the January 30 game against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Chalmers missed his first game in his two-year career. The next day, he was ruled out indefinitely with a torn ligament in his left thumb.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/01/31/chalmers.injury/|title=Heat's Chambers out indefinitely with thumb injury|access-date=June 10, 2013|date=January 31, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218065245/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/01/31/chalmers.injury/|archive-date=December 18, 2015|url-status=dead}} Chalmers returned to action on February 19 against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and played out the remainder of the season and the playoffs. ====2010–11 season==== [[File:Mario15Chalmers (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Chalmers in December 2010]] Upon the Heat's acquisition of [[LeBron James]] in July 2010, Chalmers handed over No. 6 to James after wearing it during his first two NBA seasons, and changed to his collegiate number of 15.{{cite news|last=Winderman|first=Ira|title=LeBron James gets No. 6, Mario Chalmers to wear No. 15|url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2010-07-09/sports/sfl-miami-mario-chalmers-s070910_1_mario-chalmers-heat-number-heat-center-mark-blount|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130626205443/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2010-07-09/sports/sfl-miami-mario-chalmers-s070910_1_mario-chalmers-heat-number-heat-center-mark-blount|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 26, 2013|access-date=June 9, 2011|work=Sun-Sentinel.com|date=July 9, 2010}} In Game 5 of the [[2011 NBA Finals]], Chalmers made a half-court shot at the buzzer of the first quarter to give the Heat a 31–30 lead.{{cite web|author=NBA|title=Chalmers Insane Half-Court Heave|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=glpJsnTaThk |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/glpJsnTaThk |archive-date=2021-12-15 |url-status=live|work=YouTube.com|access-date=February 27, 2013|date=February 27, 2013}}{{cbignore}} However, the Heat went on to lose the game to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] 112–103 and trailed in the series 2–3. Chalmers had 15 points, 4 rebounds, 2 assists, and 1 steal.{{cite web|title=Dallas pulls away in 4th quarter, takes 3–2 lead in Finals|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310609006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161026164355/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310609006|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 26, 2016|publisher=ESPN|date=June 9, 2011|access-date=June 9, 2011}} In Game 6, the Heat fell to the Mavericks, as they lost the series 4–2. ====2011–12 season==== On June 15, 2011, the Heat extended a qualifying offer to Chalmers, making him a restricted free agent in the offseason.{{cite web|title=HEAT Extend Qualifying Offer to Mario Chalmers|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_extend_qualifying_offer_to_mario_chalmers_2011.html|work=NBA.com|date=June 15, 2011|access-date=February 18, 2015}} On December 9, 2011, Chalmers re-signed with the Heat on a three-year, $12 million contract.{{cite web|last=Winderman|first=Ira|title=Mario Chalmers signs 3-year, $12 million Heat contract|url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2011-12-09/sports/sfl-miami-heat-mario-chalmers-s120811_1_mario-chalmers-dwyane-wade-heat-tenure|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120317232708/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2011-12-09/sports/sfl-miami-heat-mario-chalmers-s120811_1_mario-chalmers-dwyane-wade-heat-tenure|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 17, 2012|work=Sun-Sentinel.com|date=December 9, 2011|access-date=April 28, 2012}}{{cite web|title=Heat re-sign guard Mario Chalmers|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8748|work=InsideHoops.com|date=December 9, 2011|access-date=April 28, 2012}} On February 15, 2012, Chalmers was named a participant in the 2012 [[Three-Point Contest|NBA All-Star Weekend Three-Point Shootout]].{{cite web|title=Jones and Chalmers to Participate in NBA All-Star Three-Point Shootout|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/jones_chalmers_participate_allstar_shootout_2012_02_15.html|work=NBA.com|date=February 15, 2012|access-date=April 28, 2012}} He was eliminated in the first round. Chalmers was highly praised for his 25-point performance in Game 4 of the [[2012 NBA Finals]]. He scored 12 points in the fourth quarter to help the Heat win the game.{{cite web|first=Bob|last=Bajek|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1228748-nba-finals-2012-miami-heats-mario-chalmers-takes-oklahoma-city-thunder-down|title=NBA Finals 2012: Miami Heat's Mario Chalmers Comes Up Clutch in Game 4|work=BleacherReport.com|date=June 20, 2012|access-date=June 20, 2012}} In Game 5 of the NBA Finals, Chalmers recorded 10 points, seven assists, and two rebounds in 34 minutes of action as he helped the Heat win the 2012 NBA championship. It was Chalmers' first NBA title. ====2012–13 season==== On January 12, 2013, Chalmers scored a career-high 34 points against the [[Sacramento Kings]], making 10 three-pointers. He tied the Heat's record for most three-pointers in a game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/400278268/gameId/400278268/miami-heat-vs-sacramento-kings|title=Mario Chalmers has 10 3s, 34 points as Heat rough up Kings|publisher=ESPN|date=January 13, 2013|access-date=January 13, 2013}} On June 9, 2013, during Game 2 of the NBA Finals against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], Chalmers led all scorers with 19 points as the Heat tied the series 1–1 with a 103–84 victory. In the sixth game of the series, on June 18, he scored 20 points to help the Heat secure a 103–100 win. He won his second championship on June 20, as the Heat defeated the Spurs to conclude an intense seven-game series. ====2013–14 season==== On April 4, 2014, Chalmers scored a season-high 24 points in the 121–122 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140404/MINMIA/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Wolves 122, Heat 121|work=NBA.com|date=April 4, 2014|access-date=April 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160912210643/http://www.nba.com/games/20140404/MINMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=September 12, 2016|url-status=dead}} He finished the regular season with averages of 9.8 points and 4.9 assists in 73 games. The Heat advanced to the [[2014 NBA Finals]] to record their fourth straight Finals appearance. The Heat faced the San Antonio Spurs again, but unlike past Finals series, Chalmers struggled and was replaced in the starting lineup by [[Ray Allen]] in Game 5. The Heat ended up losing the series in five games. ====2014–15 season==== On July 14, 2014, Chalmers re-signed with the Heat.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-signs-mario-chalmers|title=HEAT Re-Signs Mario Chalmers|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2014|access-date=July 14, 2014}} On November 22, 2014, he scored a season-high 24 points in the 99–92 win over the Orlando Magic.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141122/MIAORL/gameinfo.html|title=Bosh, Chalmers lift Heat over Magic 99–92|work=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2014|access-date=November 22, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926092652/http://www.nba.com/games/20141122/MIAORL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=September 26, 2015|url-status=dead}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2015–2018)=== On November 10, 2015, Chalmers was traded, along with [[James Ennis (basketball)|James Ennis]], to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Jarnell Stokes]] and [[Beno Udrih]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/chalmers-and-ennis-151110|title=Grizzlies acquire Mario Chalmers and James Ennis from Heat|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 10, 2015|access-date=November 10, 2015}} He made his debut for the Grizzlies three days later, scoring 11 points off the bench in a 101–100 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151113/PORMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Randolph's putback sends Grizzlies past Portland 101–100|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 13, 2015|access-date=November 13, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330140524/http://www.nba.com/games/20151113/PORMEM/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 30, 2016|url-status=dead}} On November 16, 2015, he scored a season-high 29 points in a 122–114 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151116/OKCMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Chalmers scores 29 to led Grizzlies over Thunder 122–114|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 16, 2015|access-date=November 17, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119105903/http://www.nba.com/games/20151116/OKCMEM/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 19, 2015|url-status=dead}} On March 10, 2016, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after rupturing his right Achilles tendon in Memphis' 116–96 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]] the previous night. He was subsequently waived by the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/chalmers-injury-update-160311|title=Update on Mario Chalmers|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=March 10, 2016|access-date=March 10, 2016}} In November 2016, after recovering from the Achilles injury, Chalmers was ready to make his comeback.{{cite web|url=http://miami.cbslocal.com/2016/11/14/chalmers-hopes-comeback-chance-coming-soon/|title=Chalmers Hopes Comeback Chance Comes Soon|work=cbslocal.com|date=November 14, 2016|access-date=July 19, 2017}} However, he went unsigned throughout the 2016–17 season. On July 19, 2017, Chalmers re-signed with the Grizzlies.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/grizzlies-sign-mario-chalmers-170719|title=Grizzlies sign Mario Chalmers|work=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2017|access-date=July 19, 2017}} ===Virtus Bologna (2019)=== On March 3, 2019, Chalmers joined [[Virtus Bologna]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA), signing for the rest of the season with an option to extend it for the 2019–20 season.{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/virtus-bologna-announces-signing-of-mario-chalmers/|title=Virtus Bologna announces signing of Mario Chalmers|work=Sportando.Basketball|date=March 3, 2019|access-date=March 6, 2019|archive-date=July 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703000627/https://sportando.basketball/en/virtus-bologna-announces-signing-of-mario-chalmers/|url-status=dead}} In the 10 games he played for Virtus (including the [[Lega Basket Serie A|LBA]] and the [[Basketball Champions League|Champions League]]), he averaged 7.8 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 3 assists per game. Chalmers won the [[2018–19 Basketball Champions League|2019 FIBA Champions League]] title with Virtus. ===AEK Athens (2019–2020)=== To stay in shape, Chalmers returned to the US during the summer to join the [[Big3]] League. Charity == Chalmers is the founder of the ''Mario V. Chalmers Foundation'', which supports athletic and educational programs for children and also helps fund programs for breast cancer research. During the summer of 2012, [[Micah Lancaster]] and Chalmers directed the ''Miracle Shot Mario Chalmers'' basketball camp in [[Salina, Kansas]].{{cite web|title=Mario Chalmers Miracle Shot Basketball Camp 2015|url=http://www.mariovchalmersfoundation.org/miracle-shot-basketball-camp.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170324083639/http://www.mariovchalmersfoundation.org/miracle-shot-basketball-camp.html|archive-date=March 24, 2017|access-date=November 10, 2015|work=MarioVChlamersFoundation.org}} In 2013, Chalmers established a travel team program for youth boys called ''Team Rio National''. The U17 team is one of the top ranked teams in the nation and competes in the AAU.{{cite web|last=Jochnau|first=Garrett|date=September 23, 2013|title=Is High-Flying 7th Grader Scottie Lewis the Next Big Thing?|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1784717-is-high-flying-7th-grader-scottie-lewis-the-next-big-thing|access-date=September 23, 2013|work=BleacherReport.com}} Chalmers offers his own annual basketball camp, the Mario Chalmers Miracle Shot Basketball Camp, to help kids learn and develop basketball skills. In the past, he has hosted his camps in [[Lawrence, Kansas]], his college town, and Anchorage, Alaska, his hometown. His camp is for beginners that want to learn the fundamentals and basic skills of basketball and has a section for the more advanced players.{{Cite web|last=Skillet {{!}}
